themes_detail.label: Sudden Obstruction Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus 0.5 per week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1300% increase (z-score: 9.19)—suggesting a new, acute blockage problem affecting street access or pedestrian passage in Coney Island/Brighton Beach.
evidence: 7 obstruction complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 per week baseline (1300% spike)
Z-score of 9.19 indicates statistically extreme deviation
No prior reporting or community board discussion of obstruction issues
reporting_angles: What specific obstruction is blocking streets/sidewalks this week? (vendor overflow, construction debris, parked vehicles blocking pedestrian paths)
Has a single event (construction project, street closure, market expansion) triggered the spike?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK compared to 0.2 per week average—an 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—indicating rapid deterioration of street trees that may pose safety and visibility hazards.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 per week historical average (1100% spike)
Related spike: 3 dead/dying tree complaints 3 weeks ago (2300% spike), suggesting cumulative tree health crisis
Overgrown branches may impede pedestrian sidewalks or obstruct traffic signals
reporting_angles: Is Parks Department neglecting routine tree trimming in specific neighborhoods this spring?
Are dead/dying trees from prior weeks now becoming overgrown hazards as they're left unaddressed?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.1 per week average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—marking an unusual pollution or odor event affecting residents' outdoor environment.
evidence: 3 air quality complaints filed last week vs. 0.1 per week baseline (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No prior pattern of air quality complaints in baseline data
Timing coincides with early spring weather patterns—potential for industrial emissions, landfill odors, or marine pollution
reporting_angles: What specific pollution source triggered complaints last week? (sewage treatment, industrial facility, marine debris)
Did residents report symptoms (respiratory, nausea) or only odor/visibility issues?

themes_detail.label: Missing & Damaged Street Signs
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (missing + damaged combined) reached 7 complaints over the last 2-3 weeks—missing signs spiked to 4 LAST WEEK (700% above baseline, z-score: 4.95) and damaged signs hit 3 THREE WEEKS AGO (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)—degrading neighborhood navigation and traffic safety.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints last week vs. 0.5 per week average (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
3 damaged street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 per week average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Combined 7 sign-related complaints in 3 weeks suggests systematic neglect rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Is DOT responding to sign replacement requests? Are backlogs preventing repairs?
Are high-traffic intersections (near Cyclone, beaches, transit hubs) disproportionately affected?

themes_detail.label: Animal Incidents in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints surged to 9 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 500% spike versus 1.5 per week average (z-score: 6.71)—signaling possible wildlife management issues or increased human-animal conflict in Coney Island's public spaces.
evidence: 9 animal-in-park complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 per week historical average (500% spike)
Timing aligns with early spring (breeding season, migration period)
Coney Island's waterfront parks and boardwalk likely hotspots for wildlife encounters
reporting_angles: What animals were reported? (gulls, rats, seals, coyotes, aggressive dogs off-leash)
Are parks understaffed for animal control or wildlife management?
